senses.gloss:
conversion
------------------------------------------
The word ‘conversion’ derived from the Latin root conversio, means a change of direction, complete reorientation of one’s personality, towards God. It is a purely spiritual process of turning away from the mammon and towards God. It has nothing to do with proselytism. Identification with it is a later development.
Whether हिन्दुइस्म् has practised proselytization over the centuries or not, is a moot point. Perhaps not, at least in the aggressive sense. But there is enough evidence in the Hindu religious works indicating a quiet absorption into its folds, of aliens like the ‘yavanas’ and ‘mlecchas,’ considered to be barbaric or less civilized, whenever they have willingly adopted the Hindu ways of life. This process has gone on for almost two thousand years, often unnoticed.
But the problem which has often caused unrest in the Hindu society is that of चोन्वेर्सिओन् of the Hindus into the Semitic religions. While it has been accepted that socio-economic factors have been largely responsible for this, and efforts have been put in, to rectify the imbalances, the मिन्द् of the Hindu reli-gious leaders has also been exercised over their reconversion.
A study of the Hindu religious works, whether of the ancient ब्राह्मणस् or of the later धर्मशास्त्रस्, shows that reconversion was not an unknown pheno-menon. The sacrificial ceremonies called ‘vrātya-stomas’ were aimed at purifying and bringing back the ‘vrātyas’ (renegades as well as foreigners) into the Āryan fold. The विष्णु-dharmottara-purāṇa (A.D. 500) and the Devalasmṛti (A.D. 1000?) give specific instructions for purifying and bringing back into the Hindu fold, those who had been forcibly converted by the ‘mlecchas’ (races like the śakas, यवनस् and pahlavas). During the recent past महर्षि Dayānanda सरस्वती (A.D. 1824-1883) started the ‘śuddhi’ movement which became quite vigorous for some time.
Efforts at reconversion—often called ‘parāvartana’ or the return to the original fold—still continue. Standardization of the procedure has also been attempted at. However, the real stumbling block in the process has been the rehabilitation of the reconverted people, into the caste-conscious Hindu society.
See also PARĀVARTANA and ŚUDDHI.
